Recap
- Goal: Integrate Redwood reranker to improve search relevance for patient-facing KB and triage suggestions; target 10-15% lift in Precision@5 vs current baseline.
- Data: ~150k anonymized QA pairs + metadata fields (specialty, doc_type, date). You confirmed storage/PII constraints; you'll provide a sampled/hashed dataset for initial eval.
- Integration surface: you want minimal infra changes — use Redwood SDK where possible, with options for direct API calls if needed.

Open questions / asks for Acme (action items)

2) Confirm whether embeddings can be computed on your side (we recommend sending vectors) or if you want Redwood to host embedding generation (we can do this with tokenization-in-region).
3) Any firewall/VPC egress constraints we should know for auth and routing?

What we'll deliver (next 7 business days)

- Evaluation checklist (reranker_eval_checklist.xlsx) with recommended metrics: Precision@k, Recall@k, MRR, NDCG@k and suggested thresholds for go/no-go
- Example ranking API calls and a small sample script for top_k tuning and batch evaluation

Technical notes / preferences
- Recommended integration: developer uses Redwood embeddings endpoint OR uploads precomputed embeddings; then call Redwood's ranking API: POST /v1/ranking with candidate vectors + query vector. We typically recommend returning top_k candidates (top_k param) and running offline evaluation for k in [1,3,5,10].
- Top_k tuning: start with k=5 for UI experiments; evaluate NDCG@5 and Precision@5.
- Structured output: if you want tool-calling for downstream actions (e.g., open case, suggest doc), we can return structured JSON with action tokens; will need schema from your product team.

Thanks - attaching the plan and checklist for your review.

Hi Jordan / Priya — thanks for the quick replies. A few technical answers and suggestions: 

1) Architecture options (tradeoffs)- Option A (client-managed index): You store candidate embeddings in your vector DB (e.g., Milvus/Weaviate/FAISS). Query flow: compute query embedding -> ANN search to get N candidates (N=50 recommended) -> call Redwood /v1/ranking on the N candidate vectors to get final scores and return top_k. Pros: lower data egress, you control storage; Cons: extra infra on your side.

- Cost model: you'd pay for the ranking call size proportional to N candidates (we charge per candidate scored) plus embedding compute if done by Redwood. If you do ANN locally and pass top N to Redwood, overall cost is usually lower than passing entire corpus.

- Option B (Redwood-hosted index): We host the candidate index for you in your requested region (VPC-enabled). Flow: query -> send text or query vector -> Redwood does ANN + rerank internally then returns top_k. Pros: simplest integration, Redwood handles index ops and scaling. Cons: hosting fee + storage commitment.

2) top_k vs hybrid retrieval/rerank- We recommend a hybrid: ANN to fetch N (50) and rerank to top_k (5 or 10). For UI experiments start with top_k=5. For batch eval, compute metrics at multiple k values (1,3,5,10).

3) Eval tooling and metrics- We provide a small evaluation script that computes Precision@k, Recall@k, MRR, and NDCG@k given your labeled holdout set. I’ll attach the script to the Drive link. Suggested thresholds for a successful POC: Precision@5 >= 0.30 (relative to your baseline), NDCG@5 uplift >= 12%, MRR uplift >= 10%.

4) Auth / SDK setup- SDK: sample snippet in the attached plan. Auth: API keys scoped to the project; for VPC deployments we support mTLS and IAM-based identities. For sensitive data we recommend token rotation + KMS-backed keys.

5) Structured output / tool calling- If you want Redwood to return structured action tokens, provide a JSON schema for allowed actions; we'll map to function/tool calls. Example: {"action_type": "open_case", "fields": {"patient_id": "...", "reason": "..."}}. (We can sync with Priya on schema constraints.)

Next steps

- Priya: share schema for actions (if you want structured outputs).
- Marissa: please schedule the 30-min technical hookup for Thursday 11am PT; Vivek will join to confirm VPC/peering details.

Happy to jump on a quick call for the scoring/cost example — I can bring a notebook to run a live N=50 -> rerank demo.
